title: Treat JPYSC as account-bound until public-chain transfer is operational; separate SBI multi-rail relationships from XRP demand
decision: Represent JPYSC issuance, reserve composition, trust assets, redemption terms and transfer status as separate features.

Set public_chain_transfer_enabled=false at the current capture because SBI VC Trade explicitly says deposits and withdrawals are unavailable; do not ingest projected public-chain use cases as observed settlement.
Do not add JPYSC Lending application amounts to issued supply or verified loan balances.

Do not infer XRP demand from SBI's Circle/Arc, Open Standard/OUSD, BlackRock/JPYSC or SMFG alliances. Require actual XRPL transaction paths, XRP balances, bridge conversion and executed market/settlement evidence.
Keep legal entities separate: SBI Holdings, SBIC East Japan, SBICAH GK, Circle SBI Japan K.K., SBI Startale Marketing, SBI Ripple Asia, SBI VC Trade, SBI Shinsei Trust and Bitbank.
Treat Coinbase's Open Standard co-membership as an indirect network relationship, not a direct bilateral commercial integration with SBI.
Treat SBI's Bitbank acquisition as ownership consolidation only until orderbook, custody, liquidity and post-acquisition market-share evidence is measured.
rationale: SBI's portfolio spans Ripple/XRPL, Circle/Arc/USDC, JPYSC/Startale, Open Standard/OUSD and tokenized-MMF initiatives. However, the JPYSC distributor currently disables deposits/withdrawals, and the disclosed agreements are not production settlement evidence. Treating these relationships as automatic XRP demand would create feature leakage and causal overclaim.
alternatives_rejected: Treating all SBI-related entities as one legal counterparty.
Treating the JPYSC lending application figure as additional token supply or completed lending.
Treating shared Open Standard membership as a direct Coinbase-SBI integration.
Treating stablecoin/Arc/JPYSC growth as a proxy for XRP buying.
